title: Woodham v. South Florida Presbytery
disposition_detail: Complaint denied. The SJC rejected the claim that South Florida Presbytery lacked jurisdiction to excommunicate a Teaching Elder it had deposed and suspended; it also found no clear error in Presbytery's BCO 46-8 assignment efforts under BCO 39-3 deference. The requested annulment of the excommunication and order to assign the minister to a particular church were refused.
first_summary: The complainant challenged South Florida Presbytery's excommunication of a Teaching Elder after deposition but before assignment to a particular church under BCO 46-8. The SJC denied the complaint, holding Presbytery retained jurisdiction and did not clearly err in its BCO 46-8 efforts. Concurrences agreed in result but disputed the majority's reasoning.
summary: South Florida Presbytery deposed a Teaching Elder, suspended him from the sacraments, and later excommunicated him without first assigning him to a particular church under BCO 46-8. The complainant argued that omission stripped Presbytery of jurisdiction. The SJC denied the complaint: BCO 46-8 requires assignment but fixes no timeframe or mechanism; a deposed minister remains under Presbytery's jurisdiction until transfer, and BCO 37-9(a) preserves censure authority. Deferring under BCO 39-3, the SJC found no clear error in Presbytery's efforts. Two concurrences agreed in result but disputed the majority's broad reasoning and deference.

evidence_notes.dispute: Complainant TE Michael Woodham challenged South Florida Presbytery's August 2022 excommunication of a previously deposed and sacramentally suspended Teaching Elder without first assigning him to membership in some particular church under BCO 46-8; see lines 43-45 and issue at lines 57-59.
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: Judgment answered 'No' at lines 61-63. The adopted reasoning held Presbytery retained jurisdiction over a deposed minister, lines 77-133, and found no clear error in Presbytery's BCO 46-8 efforts under BCO 39-3 deference, lines 137-174; complaint denied at lines 176-189.
evidence_notes.qualifications: The SJC discussed and set aside the Stringer precedent in light of the later adoption of BCO 37-9, lines 112-141, and expressly made no comment on the process for excommunication, lines 120-125. Concurring opinions by RE Howie Donahoe and RE Jim Eggert are separate and not the adopted reasoning, lines 198-427.
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: No decision is incorporated by reference. Randy C. Stringer v. Mississippi Valley Presbytery, Case No. 90-7, is cited and distinguished, lines 112-114.
